name: Language navigation
summary: Use Language navigation to let users identify the current language and switch to equivalent versions offered by the service.
whenToUse: Use when the service offers equivalent content or journeys in more than one language.
Keep the switcher consistently placed and preserve journey state where the service can do so safely.
whenNotToUse: Do not show a language as available when the linked page or journey is incomplete.
Do not use country flags to represent languages.

anatomy.name: Language navigation landmark
anatomy.description: A nav has a localised aria-label describing the language choice.

anatomy.name: Language list
anatomy.description: A list contains one item for each offered language.

anatomy.name: Current language
anatomy.description: Non-link text has aria-current=true and an accurate lang attribute.

anatomy.name: Alternative links
anatomy.description: Each link uses rel=alternate, lang and hreflang for the target language.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: A small language set on a standard background.

variants.name: Inverse
variants.use: A supported dark-background location with verified contrast.

behaviour: The component requires no GOV.UK JavaScript and all alternative links must be ordinary href navigation.
Retain relevant user data across language changes only where privacy, validation and service design allow it.
Review this Trial component when updating GOV.UK Frontend because its guidance or API may change.
accessibility: Write each language name in that language and set lang so assistive technology pronounces it correctly.
Set dir on items when scripts have different writing directions.
Localise the navigation label and any visually hidden language-description text.
content: Use the native name for each language, for example “Cymraeg”.
Do not abbreviate language names unless research shows the abbreviation is understood.
Keep equivalent pages aligned so switching language does not unexpectedly change the task.
